title: Chao World: Seasons
summary: Chao World as a game of its own on the PS Vita: the Chao garden from Sonic Adventure 2: Battle, grown into a full year of seasons.
description:
Chao World: Seasons is a Chao World game made for PS Vita. It started with the Chao World inside Sonic Adventure 2: Battle: the gardens, Chao and everything you do with them, taken out of the main game and put into its own game. From there it was built out into a bigger Chao World of its own where I hope it can be a full game.

The year turns, there is Spring, Summer, Autumn and Winter, with a day/night cycle, moon phases and festivals in the lobby. I am aiming to make every Chao a unique experience, with their own personality, family, dreams and favorite things.

Chao Games, tournaments, photo pose mode, journal, status screens, decorating and new places to visit.
features: Chao World only: no story mode, every character playable
Four seasons, day and night, rainy days, falling sakura petals
Livelier Chao: personalities, families, dreams and rare Chao
The Chao Games for each season: race, karate and a swim, alone or as a team of three
Photo mode, a Chao Journal, fishing and garden decorating
New places, like the Station Square Garden and the Chao Refuge
Features from CWE
note: A fan project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by SEGA. Sonic Adventure 2, Sonic and Chao are trademarks of SEGA. Seasons runs on data from your own copy of the game, and no game files are distributed here.

title: The HVAC Trail
summary: One American summer. Five techs. 530 miles of service calls between you and Labor Day.
description:
The HVAC Trail is an Oregon Trail style survival game about running residential air conditioning calls through the hottest months of the year. Written by a working HVAC tech, tech to tech.

Pick who you are, stock the van at Big Lou's Supply House and hit the road. At every house you size up the unit, take readings or try an old trick, and make the call: a band-aid, or doing it right. Between calls, keep your crew of five hydrated and on their feet in the heat, all the way to Labor Day.
features: Diagnose real faults from the data tag, meter, amp clamp and gauges, or an old trick
Start as an owner-operator, a senior tech or a first-year apprentice
Stock up at three supply houses and paint your own van
Big jobs along the route: a McMansion, a hoarder house, a mobile home park and a lake house rental
Game Center leaderboard and a Hall of Fame
EGA DOS pixel art
Plays offline, with no account to make
note: Coming soon to the App Store.

title: Tinbox
summary: A free GBA, GB and GBC emulator for iPhone, built on the mGBA core. No ads, no accounts, no paid version.
description:
Tinbox is a native iOS emulator for GBA, GB and GBC games, with a SwiftUI interface, Metal rendering and the accurate mGBA core underneath.

It comes with two free homebrew games, keeps your library tidy, plays in portrait or landscape, and has save states, rewind, a Time Capsule that remembers your whole playthrough, a speedrun timer, RetroAchievements, themes and skins.
features: mGBA core, rendered with Metal
Save states, rewind and fast-forward
Time Capsule playthrough snapshots
Speedrun timer and RetroAchievements
Themes, skins and your own button layout
Bluetooth controller support
No ads, no accounts, nothing leaves your phone
screenshotNote: The game shown is Tobu Tobu Girl Deluxe, a free homebrew game.
note: Tinbox comes with two free homebrew games. Add games you own; it never downloads any.

title: Ekipad
status: In review for the App Store
summary: Turn your iPhone into a game controller for your Mac. Bluetooth, peer-to-peer Wi-Fi or USB, no router and no accounts.
description:
Ekipad turns your iPhone into a game controller for your Mac, styled like a Tokyo train line. It pairs with Ekipad Host, a free app for your Mac, and sends every press over Bluetooth, peer-to-peer Wi-Fi and a USB cable at once, so if one link drops, play carries on over the others. There's no router, no account and nothing sent to the internet, so it works on a plane or in a hotel too.

On macOS 15 and later your Mac sees a real Xbox controller, so Steam, SDL games, emulators and native ports just work, and game rumble buzzes the phone. For games that only take a keyboard and mouse, pick a route: WASD with mouse look, emulator layouts for one or two players, or your own mapping. Auto-switch by game changes the route by itself whenever a particular game comes to the front.

The Mouse layout turns the phone into a trackpad with big click buttons and a scroll strip, and Screen mode shows your Mac's display behind your controls. The layout editor lets you move, resize, fade and hide every button, or split A, B, X and Y into separate buttons, and gyro aiming lets you aim by tilting the phone. Up to four phones can play at once, each on its own track.

Pairing takes one click, a QR code or four pictograms, and every input is signed, so nobody nearby can pretend to be your phone. Ekipad Host is notarized by Apple and keeps itself up to date: when a new version is out, click Install and Relaunch.
features: Your Mac sees a real Xbox controller (macOS 15+)
Keyboard and mouse routes for any game, with auto-switch by game
Bluetooth, peer-to-peer Wi-Fi and USB at once, no router
Up to four phones as players 1 to 4, each in its own line colour
Mouse layout: a trackpad for your Mac, with or without Screen mode
Layout editor with split face buttons and stick click (L3/R3)
Gyro aiming and game rumble
Pair with one click, a QR code or four pictograms
Ekipad Host installs its own updates
No ads, no accounts, nothing leaves your devices
note: Ekipad needs iOS 17 or later and Ekipad Host, a free app for your Mac (macOS 14 or later; the game controller needs macOS 15). Ekipad Host comes from GitHub because the Mac App Store doesn't allow apps that create a game controller. It's signed and notarized by Apple.

title: Packmule
summary: A free file mule for iOS. Haul files between your phone and anything that speaks SMB, FTP or SFTP.
description:
Packmule moves files between your phone and Windows shares, NAS boxes, Linux machines and other phones. It can also host: start its built-in FTP server and other devices connect to the phone.

Free means free. SMB, FTP, uploads, downloads: all of it. There's no Pro tier, no subscription and no unlock. A file app shouldn't ransom your own files back to you.
features: SMB2/3 shares, FTP and SFTP
Stream movies and music straight from a share, no download first
Jellyfin: sign in, browse and stream
Built-in FTP server to host files from the phone
No ads, no subscription, no Pro tier
